scripts.title: Who should we contact first?
paragraphs: Hello everyone. We are Team Six Sigma. We studied Olist's past online orders to answer a practical question: with a limited marketing budget, which customers should we contact first?
We want to find people likely to buy again and understand who our list is missing.
scripts.transition: Let me explain how we do that.
scripts.zh: 先说经理要作的决定：预算有限，先联系谁？用历史购买行为排优先名单，并检查遗漏。不要先报算法、快照或模型文件。

scripts.title: Our approach
paragraphs: We use past purchases to make a priority list, then check who actually buys again later.
We also check which types of customers the list covers or misses. This helps a manager decide whom to contact first and which group may need a different message.
scripts.transition: Next, my teammate will explain the data behind our analysis.
scripts.zh: 先排名单，再看后来谁真的买了；再检查名单偏向哪些客户、漏了哪些客户。分群与预测的用途都保留，改成经理能理解的动作。技术划分和参数留备查及同伴展开。

scripts.title: What the results mean
paragraphs: Both January lists contained about three thousand customers. Our chosen method found fifty people who later bought again, compared with forty-six for the original method. In April, the figures were sixty-five and sixty-four. The gain was small.
Adding delivery records, reviews or customer groups did not improve the January list. But the groups did show who was being missed.
For customers who have not bought recently, we propose testing a home-goods shopping guide against a general guide. Thank you.
scripts.transition: We are happy to take your questions.
scripts.zh: 先讲观察到的差别：一月50对46、四月65对64，提升有限；已测额外特征未提高主命中。分群用于看遗漏。最后明确下一步比较家居用品主题指南与通用指南，这是提议，不是已产生的营销效果。

timing: 未真人计时，不由词数推定完成排练。

layout.text: Hello everyone. We are Team Six Sigma. We studied Olist's past online orders to answer a practical question: with a limited marketing budget, which customers should we contact first?
We want to find people likely to buy again and understand who our list is missing.
Let me explain how we do that.
We use past purchases to make a priority list, then check who actually buys again later.
We also check which types of customers the list covers or misses. This helps a manager decide whom to contact first and which group may need a different message.
Next, my teammate will explain the data behind our analysis.

Both January lists contained about three thousand customers. Our chosen method found fifty people who later bought again, compared with forty-six for the original method. In April, the figures were sixty-five and sixty-four. The gain was small.
Adding delivery records, reviews or customer groups did not improve the January list. But the groups did show who was being missed.
For customers who have not bought recently, we propose testing a home-goods shopping guide against a general guide. Thank you.
We are happy to take your questions.
